title: At gain 0.8, eight partial worm maps gave lower noise dimension than sampled degree controls in positive recurrent models
abstract: We tested how chemical wiring shapes independent noise in positive linear recurrent models of eight C. elegans brain maps. We kept 161 neurons common to all maps. Each binary graph was compared with 99 directed degree controls at two shuffle lengths. At gain 0.8, effective noise dimension was 0.355 to 0.640 of the neuron count. This was 15.0 to 49.4 percent below the long-control means. Each map was below all 99 long controls. We also tested gains 0.5 and 0.95 and count weights. Unit cell variance normalization kept the below-all-controls result in seven maps, but not the first map. These are conditional model results, not measured brain activity. Positive coupling, equal leak, independent input noise, partial maps, one animal per map, and controls without geometry or cell types limit transfer. Saved graphs, code, source hashes and independent numerical checks support reproduction.

display.caption: Effective equal-time noise dimension in positive recurrent models of eight partial worm maps. Squares show recorded wiring models. Circles and bars show means and central 95 percent ranges of 99 degree controls. All models use 161 common neurons. These are model results, not neural recordings.

citations.reason: Prior adult worm transient-growth result. We test stationary independent-noise dimension across eight developmental maps, with a new analysis and no reused code or numeric tables.
Prior site-release noise dimension result. Here independent cell noise passes through recurrent wiring; site-level shared release is absent.
